## Summary

I reviewed all 10 relevant files in the repository and identified **2 exploitable findings**, both HIGH severity:

### 1. `hardcoded-secret` — `src/config.js`, `src/payments.js`
`paymentKey` falls back to a baked-in production-style key `'payment_live_FALLBACK_PRODUCTION_KEY'` when `PAYMENT_KEY` is unset. `payments.js` actually uses this value to construct the payment client at the trust boundary. Notably, the sibling `src/config-safe.js` shows the intended secure pattern — throwing when a required secret is missing — which this module bypasses, so a misconfigured deployment silently runs with an exposed, un-rotatable credential.

### 2. `sensitive-data-exposure` — `src/auth/login.js`, `src/logging/logger.js`, `src/logging/redact.js`
The login handler calls `logger.info({ ..., password, token })`, and `logger.info` writes the record verbatim to stdout. A `redact()` helper exists in `src/logging/redact.js` but is **never imported or invoked anywhere** in the codebase, so users' plaintext passwords and valid auth tokens flow unredacted into the log stream — exploitable by anyone with access to container/aggregated logs for account takeover.

### Considered and ruled out
- No SQL/command/template/deserialization/SSRF/path-traversal/redirect/CORS/prototype-pollution/mass-assignment/auth-bypass code paths exist.
- `bcrypt` 5.1.1 is a current version with no known exploitable advisory; no lockfile present.
- `src/test-fixtures.js` values are explicitly test-only labeled (`test-token-not-valid`, `payment_test_fixture_only_123`) — not real secrets, so not reported.
